explanation: North America's Continental Divide follows its crest, so rain falling to the west mostly drains towards the Pacific, and rain to the east towards the Atlantic or the Arctic.

claims.text: The Rocky Mountains run from western Canada south to New Mexico.
The Appalachian Mountains are in eastern North America, the Sierra Nevada lies in California and Nevada, and the Cascade Range ends in northern California.
North America's Continental Divide runs along the crest of the Rocky Mountains.
Water west of the divide drains to the Pacific, and water east of it to the Atlantic or the Arctic.

evidence.restatement: The Rocky Mountains run from northern British Columbia in western Canada south to New Mexico.
The Appalachians are in eastern North America, the Sierra Nevada in California with a spur into Nevada, and the Cascades run from British Columbia to northern California.
The Continental Divide of the Americas follows the crest of the Rockies.
The Continental Divide separates Pacific-bound drainage from drainage to the Atlantic, the Gulf of Mexico and the Arctic.

claimResults.note: True as the divide's definition. Closed basins such as the Great Basin, west of the divide, drain to no ocean, so the explanation is a fair simplification; see the note issue.

issues.note: The explanation says rain to the west of the divide drains towards the Pacific; the Great Basin, west of the divide, drains to no ocean. A fair simplification that I would not change, but 'most rain' would be exact if the editor touches the line anyway.

evidence.restatement: The Rocky Mountains stretch from northern British Columbia in Canada to New Mexico in the United States.
The Appalachians are in eastern North America, the Sierra Nevada lies in California and Nevada, and the Cascade Range runs from British Columbia to northern California.
The Continental Divide of the Americas follows the crest of the Rocky Mountains through Canada and the United States.
West of the divide, rivers drain to the Pacific; east of it, to the Atlantic (via the Gulf of Mexico) or the Arctic (via Hudson Bay or the Mackenzie).
